en.p: For a real number $t$ with $t>2e$, when the function $f(x)=t(\ln x)^2-x^2$ has a local maximum at $x=k$, let $g(t)$ be the value of the real number $k$; then $g(t)$ is a differentiable function. For the real number $\alpha$ with $g(\alpha)=e^2$, when $\alpha\times\{g'(\alpha)\}^2=\dfrac{q}{p}$, find the value of $p+q$. (Here $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime natural numbers.) [4 points]
